correctness.rationale: For any specified target word, fresh i.i.d. source letters give independent geometric waiting times. Every nonempty cube has exactly one root, giving the sum T(z)/[(1-z)(1-T(z))]. T is strictly increasing on [0,1], with T(0)=0 and T(1)=q>1; its strictly positive coefficients in every degree at least three establish a unique dominant simple pole r in (0,1) and the stated residue. For f_s(x)=[x/(x+s)]^3, Lagrange stationarity of unequal positive masses implies xy=s^2; the transfer second derivative is strictly positive since f_s''(x)/(-f_s''(y))=y/x>1. Thus every maximizer has equal positive masses and value m/(1+ms)^3. At s=(cuberoot(3)-1)/3, its continuous maximum lies between m=3 and 4; the explicit rational root bounds prove the m=4 value is strictly below the m=3 value of 1. Consequently the unique all-alphabet rate maximizer has three equiprobable letters. A separate exact rational exhaustive script independently checks 115024 finite input words over six distributions. Finite experiments are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The fully inspected 2017 unrestricted subsequence-expectation paper does not treat distinct scattered cubes or sharp optimization over all alphabet supports and biases. The inspected random factor/palindrome literature treats contiguous pattern occurrence rather than these scattered cubes. Prior related exact counts or structure for special source words or different subsequence languages do not imply the present all-source equal-support rigidity theorem. Targeted searches and same-claim implication comparisons found no stronger covering result; this is bounded evidence, not a guarantee of worldwide priority.
residual_risks: A general weighted-language enumerator or power-subsequence study may already imply the result as an unstated specialization, especially in inaccessible or unindexed material.
The search and full-text corpus cannot establish worldwide novelty; independent review is not performed.

value.rationale: Cube words constitute a natural repetition language important to word combinatorics; counting distinct target strings rather than embeddings is a meaningful source complexity invariant. The theorem supplies a complete exact mean generating function at every fixed source and determines the nontrivial sharp global exponential optimizer, including a rigorous classification of its support across all finite alphabet sizes. The optimizer differs from the four-symbol optimizer for scattered palindromic means, revealing language-sensitive source diversity. This is not a textbook substitution, tiny numerical improvement, or unsupported sequence-table claim.
